column1: # sources.tsv: where each header of the sysroot comes from (read by build-headers.sh, next to this file)
# One row per file, tab-separated, sorted in byte order (LC_ALL=C sort), no empty field:
#   kind        hdr = a file installed into the sysroot; in = a further input that the processing
#               reads (.defs files for mig, the sources of mig itself), placed in the work directory
#   path        hdr: path in the sysroot; in: path in the work directory
#   repo        repository at https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/, or "own" (a file of this
#   commit      the commit of that tag (own: -); build-headers.sh fetches by commit
#   file        path of the file in that release (own: path below this directory)
#   sha256      of that file, as published (own: of our file); checked before it is used
#   processing  RULE, optionally followed by +patch:NAME (patches/NAME) once or more. Rules:
#               none, libc, xnu, xnu-bsd-sys, xnu-4570, carbon, mig; build-headers.sh describes each.
# The set of hdr rows is an allow-list: build-headers.sh installs exactly these files and nothing
# else, because the compiler and libc++ probe for headers (__has_include) and a file that exists
# changes what they compile. A header is added when a source of the build needs it, from a published
# release where one exists: the closest published version of that file, processed by the rule of the
# release's own install step; a patch of ours only where no published version gives the same
# object files; a file under own/ only where Apple never published one. Then run
# "build-headers.sh --update-pins OUTDIR", review the change of HEADERS.sha256, and compare the build
